questions.q: What does InnoDB tablespace encryption protect against?
options: Data being read from a stolen physical disk, snapshot, or backup file
A legitimately authenticated query reading the table normally
Network interception of query traffic
SQL injection attacks
questions.explain: MySQL decrypts transparently for any privileged query, so at-rest encryption does not protect against authenticated reads — only against access outside the running server.

questions.q: What SQL clause enables encryption on a new InnoDB table?
options: ENCRYPTION = 'Y' in the CREATE TABLE statement
REQUIRE SSL in the CREATE TABLE statement
SET GLOBAL innodb_encryption = ON
GRANT ENCRYPT ON the table
questions.explain: ENCRYPTION = 'Y' can be set on CREATE TABLE or added later with ALTER TABLE, provided a keyring plugin is configured.

questions.q: What does setting require_secure_transport = ON in my.cnf do?
options: Forces every connection to the server to use TLS, rejecting plaintext connection attempts
Encrypts InnoDB tablespace files on disk
Removes anonymous user accounts
Enables the validate_password component
questions.explain: This is the server-wide setting for encryption in transit, distinct from at-rest tablespace encryption.

questions.q: What's the difference between REQUIRE SSL and REQUIRE X509 on a user account?
options: REQUIRE X509 additionally requires the client to present a valid certificate signed by a trusted CA, for mutual authentication
They are functionally identical
REQUIRE SSL is stronger than REQUIRE X509
REQUIRE X509 only applies to root accounts
questions.explain: REQUIRE SSL mandates an encrypted connection; REQUIRE X509 goes further and requires genuine mutual TLS authentication.

questions.q: If a server has InnoDB tablespace encryption enabled but require_secure_transport is off and no account has REQUIRE SSL set, what risk remains?
options: Data in transit over the network can still be intercepted unencrypted, since at-rest encryption doesn't cover network traffic
No risk remains, since at-rest encryption covers all cases
The tablespace encryption itself would fail to work without TLS also enabled
Anonymous accounts would automatically be re-created
questions.explain: At-rest and in-transit encryption are separate mechanisms; enabling one does not provide the protection of the other.
